newsitem.title: USA: NYS speaker says no alternatives to LILCO pact.
newsitem.headline: NYS speaker says no alternatives to LILCO pact.

text.p: The New York Assembly Speaker on Tuesday said there were no alternatives to Governor George Pataki's plan to partly takeover the Long Island Lighting Co , adding he thought his conditions would be met.

"There are no other alternatives here, it's a matter of making the deal that's on the table better," Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, told reporters shortly before joining the Republican governor and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, for a leaders' meeting.

However, the Assembly Speaker said that he did not expect any agreement on having the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) buy assets from LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas, which plan to merge, would break a logjam on the state's budget, which was due on April 1.
Silver added that a letter to the governor outlining his conditions had been sent, and that staffers had signaled they thought it would be possible to reach an accord.

Silver, Pataki and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, each hold one of three seats on the state Public Authorities Control Board, which must approve tax-exempt bond sales. The board next is scheduled to meet on Wednesday, and the LIPA plan is on the agenda.
Newsday, in its Tuesday edition, said Silver was seeking assurances from the governor that included getting the parties to guarantee, in writing, how much rates will drop over the next 10 years.

And Silver told Newsday he wants LILCO, which plans to merge with Brooklyn Union Gas, to assure the state it will spend at least half the money it is paid for its assets on developing Long Island's energy infrastructure.

Much of the savings produced under the governor's plan rely on the tax-exempt bond sale--the nation's largest--and the Internal Revenue Service would have to hold that LILCO shareholders were not subject to a $2 billion capital gains tax for the deal to go forward. The federal tax agency was expected to soon publish new rules governing how such transactions are treated.
